response.answer: Anomaly detection methods fit probability distributions over manually annotated data to flag deviations as likely errors, enhancing corpus quality assurance and error correction. Techniques include PCA and clustering. Evaluation metrics like F1 score are used.

results.title: [PDF] Annotation Error Detection - arXiv
results.content: Annotation Error Detection: Analyzing the Past and Present for a More Coherent Future Jan-Christoph Klie∗ Ubiquitous Knowledge Processing Lab Department of Computer Science Technical University of Darmstadt www.ukp.tu-darmstadt.de Bonnie Webber School of Informatics, University of Edinburgh Iryna Gurevych UKP Lab / TU Darmstadt Annotated data is an essential ingredient in natural language processing for training and evaluating machine learning models. It is therefore very desirable for the annotations to be of high quality. Recent work, however, has shown that several popular datasets contain a surprising amount of annotation errors or inconsistencies. To alleviate this issue, many meth-ods for annotation error detection have been devised over the years. While researchers show that their approaches work well on their newly introduced datasets, they rarely compare their methods to previous work or on the same datasets. We therefore reimplement 18 methods for detecting potential annotation errors and evaluate them on 9 English datasets for text classiﬁcation as well as token and span labeling.
